data.title: Darier's disease — viva
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Darier's disease** (Genodermatoses)_

**Q1. What is Darier's disease (keratosis follicularis)?**
- Autosomal dominant genodermatosis due to ATP2A2 mutations (SERCA2 — sarco/endoplasmic reticulum Ca²⁺-ATPase) → impaired desmosome assembly → acantholysis and dyskeratosis; onset around puberty (10–20 y)

**Q2. Clinical features.**
- Greasy, warty, red-brown keratotic papules in a seborrhoeic distribution — scalp margin, forehead, nasolabial folds, ears, central chest/back, flexures (may become vegetating and malodorous); itchy, worse with heat, sweat, UV and friction
- Acral: palmar pits/punctate keratoses, AKV-like papules on dorsa of hands
- Nails (diagnostic): longitudinal alternating red and white bands, V-shaped notching at the free edge, subungual hyperkeratosis
- Oral: cobblestone white papules on palate
- Neuropsychiatric associations: depression, bipolar disorder, epilepsy, intellectual disability; salivary gland obstruction
- Variants: segmental/linear (mosaic), haemorrhagic acral, comedonal, bullous

**Q3. Histopathology.**
- Suprabasal acantholysis forming clefts (lacunae) with villi, dyskeratotic cells — corps ronds (large round cells with pyknotic nucleus and clear halo, in spinous/granular layers) and grains (small elongated dark cells in stratum corneum), column of parakeratosis over the clefts
- DIF negative (vs pemphigus)

**Q4. Complications.**
- Secondary bacterial infection, Kaposi's varicelliform eruption (HSV), dermatophyte infections, malodour, social stigma

**Q5. Differential diagnosis.**
- Seborrhoeic dermatitis, Hailey–Hailey (flexural, erosions, no nail bands), Grover's disease (transient acantholytic dermatosis — older men, trunk, transient), acanthosis nigricans, confluent and reticulated papillomatosis, AKV of Hopf, pemphigus vegetans, warts

**Q6. Management.**
- Avoid triggers: heat, sweating, sun (sunscreen), friction; cool cotton clothing; antiseptic washes
- Topical: retinoids (tazarotene, adapalene), steroids (short courses), 5-FU, calcineurin inhibitors, antibiotics/antifungals for infections
- Systemic: acitretin 10–25 mg/day or isotretinoin (most effective); doxycycline for flares; antivirals for HSV; oral magnesium chloride (case reports)
- Procedures: CO2/Er:YAG laser ablation, dermabrasion, PDT, excision for localised hypertrophic areas; botulinum toxin for flexural sweat-induced flares

## Quick spotter facts
- Greasy warty papules in seborrhoeic distribution + red/white nail bands with V-nicks — Darier's (ATP2A2)
- Corps ronds and grains

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (Darier's disease). Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
